newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Loewen Group busy after bid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Loewen Group busy after bid.

text.p: Loewen Group Inc options were active on the Chicago Board Options Exchange and volatilities surged as investors digested a takeover bid for the company announced earlier this week.

On Monday, Service Corp International launched a bid for the Canadian-based funeral home operator in a stock swap valuing it at $43 per share. Loewen said it would review the bid and respond in due course.
Following the bid, Loewen shares gapped open at 42-1/2 compared with an intraday high of 34-1/8 on Monday but never reached the $43 bid price, reflecting wariness about the bid.
On Wednesday, Service Corp said its board of directors ratified its proposed acquisition.
At 1120 CDT (1620 GMT) Thursday, Loewen Group shares were up 2-1/4 at 42, their best level of the session.
Few of the Loewen September options traded this week and interest in the October series was relatively thin until Thursday, when the October 35, 40 and 45 calls and puts were busy.
On Tuesday, 2,100 of the October 40 calls traded, in two blocks of 1,000 and one of 100. All that activity was from spreads. About 550 traded on Wednesday.
By 1120 CDT Thursday the October 40 call traded 127 contracts. Its open interest was up to about 2,400.
The October 35 call, with open interest of 45, traded 1,200 contracts. The October 45 call, active on Tuesday and Wednesday, traded 80 contracts.
"There's a lot of interest in purchasing the October 40-45 call spread," said Jim Gelbort, a designated primary market maker at Tague Securities Corp in Chicago.
He said the January 1997 40-45 call spread was also popular. Five hundred of the January 40 calls traded and 430 of the January 45 calls traded.
"We've found some outright sellers of the October 40 and 45 puts," he added. The Loewen Group October 40 puts traded more than 2,200 contracts and the October 45 puts traded 1,325.
The October 40 call had open interest of about 230 and the October 45 had open interest around 10.
Gelbort said implied volatilities on the Loewen Group options were up around 40 percent over the last two days.
"Our feeling is that now that the stock is in play, it could take a while to sort everything out and to find out what the company's intentions are," he said.
Only four Service Corp options, which trade on the Philadelphia Stock Exchange, were traded.
The September 30 call traded 62 contracts, the November 30 call traded 24, the February 1997 22-1/2 call traded two and the February 30 call traded eight.
Service Corp shares were up 1/4 at 30-5/8.
--Gregory Crawford, derivatives desk, (312) 408-8750
